newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Longer OLOs to stay on players' shopping list.
newsitem.headline: Longer OLOs to stay on players' shopping list.

text.p: The longer end of the Belgian government bond yield curve stands to benefit most from the near-term action, dealers said on Tuesday, with buyers back at that part of the curve after recent attention for the short end.

"The long end is flattening again," a trader said, expecting the trend to continue at least until Friday when the OLO market expects fresh clues on the course of U.S. interest rates, and consequently its own direction, from U.S. inflation numbers.
Volumes were expected to remain unexciting, though, with many end-investors not keen to come in at current levels or take profits already.

The yields on the 2012 (282) and 2015 (262) OLOs eased by some five basis points over the past week, slightly lagging the 10-year benchmark 286 BE298= and quite notably falling behind five-year paper.

Recently, cash had been going into the short end in the wake of the U.S. Fed's recent rate rise, but the upward scope there had faded now. The focus should pan to the longer end, especially after today's OLO exchange auction, dealers said.
Totalling over 21 billion francs -- almost double the last auction's volume -- the swap was deemed a reasonable success. As expected the bulk went in the 10-year benchmark.
Dealers said there was now scope for the 10-year yield to go below 6.00 percent again, although some were sceptical it would fall much below that psychological level.

Re-training their sights on low inflation and interest rates, players could push the yield to 5.80 or 5.85 percent in the next one or two months, some said. Other have targetted levels at around 5.90 percent by the end of the second quarter.
The benchmark bond yielded 6.03 percent in late Tuesday trade, unchanged from late Monday levels.
Dealers said OLOs had held up well in the face of the usual pre-auction pressure and the soft tone on the key German market.
Bunds came under pressure after news that German unemployment fell slightly in March, reversing some of the gains posted on Monday on talk of a more sizeable fall.
Dealers now expected the OLO market to remain relatively quiet until Friday when U.S. inflation data are due.

U.S. March PPIs are forecast to come in slightly firmer month-on-month, but easier year-on-year on the back of the dollar's strength, which will have capped imported inflation. Retail sales numbers are expected to show growth slowed in March compared with February, which should give bonds further support.
